newsitem.title: CHINA: China's children suffer from school stress.
newsitem.headline: China's children suffer from school stress.

text.p: Heavy school workloads, emphasis on test results and competition with other students are creating psychological problems for many Chinese schoolchildren, the Guangming Daily said on Friday.
A nationwide survey of children aged 4-16 years had showed 13.9 percent suffered psychological problems, the newspaper said.
Outdated teaching methods that focused on heavy homework loads and test results were some of the main causes of students' anxieties, it said.
"Every day from morning to evening primary and middle school students do only one thing -- wrestle with books," it said.
"The two days of rest are also filled with extra-curricular classes so that there is nearly no time for fun, games or work," it said of the nation's students.
Pressure by parents and teachers to succeed had heaped more stress on students, it said.
Chinese children are placed in nurseries and kindergartens often by the time they are three years old.
The survey had found that of 2,300 students in one middle school in Nanjing in eastern Jiangsu province, 67 percent had difficulty coping with failure, it said.
Pressure on Chinese students has mounted in recent years as competition for entry into universities becomes more fierce. Many parents force their children to take extra classes at weekends.
